152	## 4. Make it amazing
153	
154	These are the big bets, each built on something Ward already has.
155	
156	1. **Context-aware reading on every phone (Ward Lite v2).** Today most children get packs plus Ward Lite reading one message at a time. That setup flags 60% of hard negatives and reads 12 of 14 help-seekers as bullies. Use E4B second-look verdicts on synthetic group chats (`gen-synthetic.ts`, `gen-contrast.ts`) as labels, and add "reported speech" and "mutual banter" heads. Ship only if dangerous recall (18/38 today) doesn't drop. Publish the before and after numbers the way the 25%-to-5% fix was published.
157	
158	2. **Ward reads what children actually see.** The Android share target already accepts images (`AndroidManifest.xml:30,36`). The phone already runs Gemma 4 E2B through LiteRT-LM. Add image and short-audio input, plus a text-recognition fallback, so Instagram DMs and Pakistani voice notes become evidence the child confirms before saving.
159	
160	3. **The intake layer for helplines.** ward.report/v2, the offline viewer and the CSV export exist. Co-design v3 with DRF caseworkers, add device signing, and produce takedown packets a helpline with priority channels can forward. DRF's 3,012 complaints in 2025, with cases involving minors up 28%, mean intake time is a real bottleneck.
161	
162	4. **"Ward and the Ghosts": the series is the curriculum.** The 21 tested branching stories, seven units, Class mode and the school kit are already a script bible. Each episode ends on a story's choice point, and a QR code opens that exact story in the app. The reel drives into the branching experience instead of answering for the child. Add an "episode" slide to Class mode. (Details in section 5.)

258	Each question has my recommended answer.
259	
260	### A. Safety policy
261	
262	1. **Should a lone severity-3 message that only Ward Lite caught ever be quietly demoted to "unsure"?**
263	   Recommended: never hide severity 3. In a 1:1 chat, treat it as urgent. Elsewhere, show the full help block labelled "unconfirmed" and include it in the report with `confirmed: false`.
264	2. **Should an unconfirmed danger show the full red help block or a softer "just in case" version?**
265	   Recommended: the same helplines and Take It Down, under the softer heading already built. A reviewer signs off the wording.
266	3. **Should "unsure" messages be excluded from a helpline report?**
267	   Recommended: no. Put them in a separate, clearly labelled "unconfirmed" section.
268	4. **Should Discord server mode exist under the "never alert adults" commitment?**
269	   Recommended: relabel it as a moderator tool with its own policy section, keep it off by default until review, and never nudge on dangerous messages.
270	5. **Where, if anywhere, should children's corrections go before a lead and a pilot exist?**
271	   Recommended: nowhere. The file stays on the device.
272	6. **Which safe-messaging guidance should Ward follow?**
273	   Recommended: the WHO 2023 media guidance, adapted with the reviewing helpline's own guidance.
274	7. **Should flagged words be hidden by default?**
275	   Recommended: for the 8-10 band, and for self-harm, sexual and exposure messages at every age, with a toggle on the Me screen.
276	8. **Should there be a vault recovery code?**
277	   Recommended: yes, opt-in. The child chooses who holds it, and Ward suggests a trusted adult.
278	9. **Keep phone-to-family-computer pairing?**
279	   Recommended: yes, with remote Gemma set to raise-only and honest copy now, and token pairing later.
280	10. **Should counsellor mode stay in the child's app, and are counsellor PCs shared school machines?**
281	    Recommended: assume shared machines, so give counsellor mode a separate passphrase. Gate it now, and move it to a separate build later.
282	11. **Should the adult side ever receive anything the child didn't actively send, even in a dangerous case?**
283	    Recommended: no. This closes off the most-requested parent feature, so it should be your call.
284	
285	### B. The campaign
286	
287	12. **Who is the primary audience per platform?**
288	    Recommended: teens 13+ on TikTok, Reels and Shorts; parents and teachers on Facebook and WhatsApp; 8-12 via made-for-kids YouTube and classrooms.
289	13. **Gate install calls to action until a review?**
290	    Recommended: yes (wave 1, then wave 2).
291	14. **Which countries first?**
292	    Recommended: Pakistan, then India with Hinglish. Bangladesh after Bangla improves.
293	15. **What does your reels factory take as input (script JSON, storyboard, voice files), at what length and style, and does it lip-sync Urdu?**
294	    Recommended: 30 to 60 seconds, 9:16, chat-on-screen with the ghost, humans shown as hands and phones only.
295	16. **Which four episodes to pilot?**
296	    Recommended: E1, E4, E6, E8.
297	17. **Make E10 (sextortion) in wave 1?**
298	    Recommended: no. Wave 2, 13+ feeds only.
299	18. **Who moderates comments?**
300	    Recommended: two adults, with comments off on E6, E10 and E11.
301	19. **Who is your native Urdu reviewer, and should the videos use the app's voice?**
302	    Recommended: yes, the same voice, recorded in one session.
303	20. **Should there be a separate made-for-kids YouTube channel?**
304	    Recommended: yes.
305	21. **Which targets matter most?**
306	    Recommended: schools and helplines engaged, ahead of installs.
307	
308	### C. Release and distribution
309	
310	22. **Who holds the signing keystore, and where are the backups?**
311	    Recommended: you, with two offline backups and a second custodian.
312	23. **Should v0.1.0 ship before the submission deadline?**
313	    Recommended: only after the ONNX fix is verified on a real phone, labelled "preview". If that slips past the deadline, the README says "build from source" in the meantime.
314	24. **Should the default APK be the lite flavour without phone Gemma?**
315	    Recommended: yes. Offer Gemma as a second download.
316	25. **Host a try-it-in-the-browser demo, and on which domain?**
317	    Recommended: yes, a github.io address first, with a strict CSP and framed as a demo.
318	26. **Publish on Google Play as an individual or an organisation?**
319	    Recommended: wait for the organisation. Choose "use my own key" at enrollment, because it can't be undone.
320	27. **Budget for code signing (Apple Developer, SignPath)?**
321	    Recommended: apply to SignPath now (free for open source); buy the Apple account when funded.
322	28. **Is an opt-in, tap-only update check acceptable?**
323	    Recommended: yes, tap-only, never automatic.
324	29. **Where should models be hosted?**
325	    Recommended: a Hugging Face org with pinned hashes, and GitHub Releases as a mirror for the phone model.
326	30. **Should there be an official Discord instance, and who pays?**
327	    Recommended: not until review. Personal mode only when it launches.
328	31. **Is iOS in scope for 2027?**
329	    Recommended: not yet. Ship a PWA first and fix the iPhone copy now.
330	32. **Device builds on every push, or nightly?**
331	    Recommended: Android on path-filtered pushes, desktop nightly.
332	33. **Which low-end reference phone?**
333	    Recommended: a real 32-bit Android Go phone with 2 to 3 GB of RAM, from the pilot city.
334	
335	### D. People and partners
336	
337	34. **Do you have a contact at DRF, Madadgaar or Rozan, and will you make the approach?**
338	    Recommended: approach DRF first, asking for script review and report feedback.
339	35. **Will you hand the safeguarding lead role to a partner organisation?**
340	    Recommended: yes, independent of the helpline that receives reports, with an honorarium.
341	36. **Can you reach native speakers for Urdu, Hinglish and Bangla, and is a paid-reviewer budget realistic?**
342	    Recommended: 2 to 3 per language, paid per item.
343	37. **Do you have, or want, an academic partner for ethics and the evaluation design?**
344	    Recommended: yes, through a university psychology department.
345	38. **Which city and schools for the pilot?**
346	    Recommended: one city, 3 to 5 schools, including a girls' school and a low-fee school.
347	39. **Who writes the per-band wording?**
348	    Recommended: pilot teachers draft it, and a child-protection reviewer signs it off.
349	40. **Who signs off helpline changes?**
350	    Recommended: the safeguarding lead. Until then, you, with a dated source for each number.
351	41. **Which countries should the helpline list add first?**
352	    Recommended: UAE and Saudi Arabia, then Ireland, Nepal and Canada.
353	42. **Could a pilot school let 14-17 year olds run sessions for younger classes?**
354	    Recommended: yes, in groups with a named adult.
355	
356	### E. Money, legal and scope
357	
358	43. **Registered entity in Pakistan, or a fiscally hosted open-source project?**
359	    Recommended: a fiscal host now (for example Open Source Collective), with a partner NGO as data controller for pilots.
360	44. **How much time can you commit after the hackathon?** Only you can answer this, and the whole plan depends on it.
361	45. **Content licence for lessons, stories, the kit and videos?**
362	    Recommended: CC BY 4.0, the easiest for schools and NGOs. CC BY-SA 4.0 is the alternative if you want adaptations to stay open.
363	46. **Which ElevenLabs plan generated the 107 clips?**
364	    Recommended: check its terms. If it was the free plan, regenerate the clips with an open voice.
365	47. **Who is the DPG authorised representative?**
366	    Recommended: you, until an organisation exists.
367	48. **Change the README headline before the deadline, even if honest wording costs some "wow"?**
368	    Recommended: yes.
369	49. **Phone screenshots: build them now, or say honestly that they're not on phones yet?**
370	    Recommended: the honest message now, and build later.
371	50. **Allow a school-level aggregation step for slang?**
372	    Recommended: yes later, with a minimum count of children per word and a privacy reviewer.
373	51. **Generate a device key for signed reports?**
374	    Recommended: yes in v3, worded as "signed by this Ward install", never as proof of what was said.
375	
376	---

input.script:
export const meta = {
  name: 'ward-series-pilots',
  description: 'Write the four pilot Ward episodes in Roman Urdu (kids and teen cuts), review for safeguarding and language, revise',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Write', detail: 'one writer per episode, both cuts' },
    { title: 'Review', detail: 'safeguarding and Roman Urdu reviewers per episode' },
    { title: 'Revise', detail: 'the writer\'s pass on both reviews' },
  ],
}

const REPO = '/Users/haider/Desktop/Hacktoberfest 26/ward'
const OUT = '/Users/haider/Desktop/Hacktoberfest 26/ward-series'
const AUDIT = '/Users/haider/Desktop/Hacktoberfest 26/ward-audit-2026-10-31.md'
const REELS = '/Users/haider/Projects/reel-factory'

const BRIEF = `You are writing a short animated story episode about Ward, a free open-source app that is a small, friendly ghost on a child's side against cyberbullying ("The bully is the ghost haunting the chat. Ward is the ghost on your side."). The owner wants to see ROMAN URDU scripts first (Pakistani kids' and teens' Roman Urdu as they actually text and talk, e.g. "yaar", "scene", "chill", code-mixed English where natural; not formal Urdu transliterated word for word).

Read first:
- ${AUDIT}, section 5 "Spreading the word" (episode table, safeguarding rules for videos 1-10, wave 1 rules). Do not copy anything else from it anywhere.
- The source stories in ${REPO}/packages/lessons/src/stories.ts and stories.ur.ts (and units.ts for the unit's lesson).
- ${REELS}/docs/story-scenes.md and ${REELS}/README.md: the reels are made by the owner's local reel factory: 1080x1920, about 30-45 seconds (~70-110 spoken words), "theme": "story" scenes with bean-people characters (moods, poses, speech bubbles of at most 6 words), sets (room, night, city, stage, island, office, lab, cyber), props (phone, lock, shield, magnifier...), kinetic captions from the narration. There is no ghost character yet: describe Ward as a small, soft, white friendly ghost with a warm glow and simple face (a new cast kind the owner will add), using moods like worried, calm, cheer.

Rules (non-negotiable, from the audit's video rules and Ward's safeguarding policy):
1. Wave 1: kids' cuts and teen cuts end on a behaviour, never "download/install Ward". Example endings: "Reply mat karo. Screenshot lo, phir block." / "Ek bade ko batao."
2. Never claim Ward "protects" or "keeps kids safe". Ward helps you notice, keep proof and decide who to tell.
3. No slurs; use the story's mildest lines. No self-harm content. No methods. No sexual content. No real app logos or interfaces (fictional "Blocktown", "7B group" etc.).
4. The viewer ("tum"/"aap" addressed in narration) must never be gendered: use imperatives and neutral constructions (Urdu verbs agree with gender: avoid "tum kar sakte/sakti ho", "main gaya/gayi" for the viewer or the reader-character; prefer "karo", "kar lo", "chaho to", نے-constructions).
5. Every episode ends with an end card: "Ward kisi ko kuch nahi batata, isliye tum khud chuno kis bade ko batana hai" (or a natural equivalent) plus helplines: Pakistan Madadgaar 1098 first, DRF Cyber Harassment Helpline 0800-39393 (weekdays 9 to 5), India/Bangladesh 1098, findahelpline.com elsewhere.
6. No "follow for part 2" or engagement pressure in the kids' cut.
7. Kids' cut (8-12, classroom and made-for-kids YouTube): gentle, slower, simpler words, the question frozen on screen so a class can vote ("Tum kya karte? A, B ya C?" phrased neutrally), then the kind ending.
   Teen cut (13-17, TikTok/Reels/Shorts): a hook in the first 2 seconds, faster, Roman Urdu chat bubbles on a phone, real teen voice, never preachy.

Write ONE markdown file for your episode at the path given, containing for EACH cut:
- Title, cut (kids or teen), platform, length, source story id and unit.
- The hook (first line on screen).
- NARRATION in Roman Urdu (the voiceover, ~70-110 words), then an English gloss in italics, line by line.
- Scene-by-scene beats as a table: # | set | who's on stage (cast, mood, pose) | speech bubbles (Roman Urdu, at most 6 words each) | on-screen text/props | cue phrase from the narration.
- The call to action (behaviour) and the end card text.
- A short "safeguarding notes" list: what you deliberately left out and why.
- "For the voice": tone and pace notes for whoever records it (the owner will likely record it themself; no ElevenLabs credits).
Keep everything warm, specific and honest.`

const EPISODES = [
  { key: 'e1', file: 'E1-ward-on-your-side.md', ask: 'Episode E1 "The ghost on your side": who Ward is, in one story beat. Kids cut: a child gets a mean message in a class group, Ward appears as a soft glow and helps them notice, save it and tell someone. Teen cut: the hook line "The bully is the ghost haunting the chat. Ward is the ghost on your side." in Roman Urdu, a pile-on in a group chat, Ward lights up what is happening and the teen keeps proof and picks one person to tell. Mention that Ward runs on the phone and keeps their chats private only in plain words, without overclaiming.' },
  { key: 'e4', file: 'E4-shut-it-down.md', ask: 'Episode E4 "Shut it down: don\'t feed it". Kids cut from the story "the-treehouse" (8-10, a player wrecks your build in a game and says "cry about it"): don\'t reply, save it, block, tell. Teen cut from a 13+ appropriate story in the "stop" unit (e.g. "secret-fan" adapted to 13+, or another stop story; NOT "one-hour", which is wave 2 only): replying feeds it, keep proof, block and report.' },
  { key: 'e6', file: 'E6-say-it.md', ask: 'Episode E6 "Say it": the real reason children don\'t tell. Kids cut from "the-tablet-worry" (fear that telling means losing the tablet; Ammi, Khala or Ms Farah). Teen cut from "the-other-group" or "just-ignore-it" (telling one adult didn\'t work, so tell another; don\'t let one adult be the last). Both end on "ek bade ko batao" in a natural way.' },
  { key: 'e8', file: 'E8-back-them-up.md', ask: 'Episode E8 "Back them up": upstanding, privately. Kids cut from "mias-drawing" (Mia\'s drawing gets laughed at; send one kind message privately). Teen cut from "the-poll" (a poll mocking Ayesha\'s voice cracking at the talent show; don\'t vote, don\'t share, message Ayesha privately, report the poll).' },
]

const REVIEW = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    verdict: { type: 'string', enum: ['good', 'revise'] },
    issues: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: { where: { type: 'string' }, problem: { type: 'string' }, suggestion: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['where', 'problem', 'suggestion'] } },
  },
  required: ['verdict', 'issues'],
}

const results = await pipeline(
  EPISODES,
  (e) => agent(`${BRIEF}\n\nYOUR EPISODE: ${e.ask}\n\nWrite the file to ${OUT}/${e.file} (create the folder if needed). Write nothing anywhere else, and never inside ${REPO}. Reply with a two-line summary.`, { label: `write:${e.key}`, phase: 'Write' }),
  (_w, e) => parallel([
    () => agent(`You are a child-safeguarding reviewer (think: a helpline's content lead) checking a short animated video script for children and teens about cyberbullying. Read ${OUT}/${e.file} and the rules in ${AUDIT} section 5 "Safeguarding rules for the videos". Check: no install call to action (wave 1), no "Ward protects you" claims, no slurs, no self-harm or sexual content, nothing that shames or blames the viewer, upstanding stays safe and private, the end card has the right helplines (Madadgaar 1098 first, DRF 0800-39393 weekdays 9 to 5, India/Bangladesh 1098, findahelpline.com), age-fit tone for each cut, no engagement pressure in the kids' cut, no real platform logos. Read-only.`, { label: `review-safe:${e.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: REVIEW }),
    () => agent(`You are a native speaker of Pakistani Urdu who knows how Pakistani kids (8-12) and teens (13-17) really talk and text in Roman Urdu. Read ${OUT}/${e.file}. Check: does the Roman Urdu sound natural and current (not stiff, not translated-from-English, not cringe), is the spelling consistent and readable for kids, are speech bubbles at most 6 words, is the viewer and the main child never gendered by verb agreement (e.g. "kar sakta/sakti", "gaya/gayi", "thak gaya" for the viewer), do the narration and bubbles fit 30-45 seconds (~70-110 words), and does the English gloss match. Read-only.`, { label: `review-lang:${e.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: REVIEW }),
  ]).then((reviews) => ({ reviews: reviews.filter(Boolean) })),
  (rv, e) => {
    const issues = rv.reviews.flatMap((r) => r.issues)
    if (!issues.length) return { key: e.key, file: e.file, revised: false, issues: 0 }
    return agent(`${BRIEF}\n\nYou wrote ${OUT}/${e.file} for: ${e.ask}\n\nTwo reviewers (safeguarding; Roman Urdu) raised these points. Revise the file in place to address the real ones; at the end of the file add a short "Review notes" section listing what you changed and anything you disagreed with and why. Reply with a two-line summary.\n\n${JSON.stringify(issues, null, 2)}`, { label: `revise:${e.key}`, phase: 'Revise' }).then((s) => ({ key: e.key, file: e.file, revised: true, issues: issues.length, summary: s }))
  },
)
return results

questions.question: A dangerous-sounding message only Ward Lite caught, in a group chat, with nothing around it backing it up: how should Ward treat it? (In one-to-one chats it's now always urgent.)

options.label: Full help, unconfirmed (Recommended)
options.description: Same helplines, Coach and Take It Down as urgent, under the softer "not sure" heading; it goes in the report in a labelled "unconfirmed" section. Never hidden.

options.label: As now
options.description: "Not sure" heading with helplines on screen, but no Coach, and kept out of the report.

options.label: Always urgent
options.description: Treat it like any dangerous message: red verdict, in the report. More false alarms in group chats.

questions.question: Discord server mode alerts moderators, which breaks the written promise that Ward never alerts adults. What should it be?

options.label: Moderator tool, off (Recommended)
options.description: Relabel it a moderator tool with its own policy section, default off until a safeguarding review, alerts carry a link and category only for self-harm, and members see a pinned notice.

options.label: Remove it
options.description: Ship personal mode only (check, save evidence, report, help). Simplest to defend.

options.label: Keep as is
options.description: Leave it on as built and update the safeguarding docs to say so.

options.label: Preview after phone test (Recommended)
options.description: Once the Ward Lite build fix is verified on a real phone, tag v0.1.0 labelled preview. Needs your signing keystore and the four GitHub secrets first. README says "build from source" until then.

options.label: Build from source only
options.description: No release for now; the README and the Give screen point to building from source.

options.label: Tag now, debug-signed
options.description: Fastest, but a later properly signed release can't update it: users would have to uninstall, which wipes the vault.

questions.question: For the videos: should install calls to action wait for a safeguarding reviewer's sign-off (wave 1 teaches behaviours only)?

options.label: Yes, two waves (Recommended)
options.description: Wave 1 now: episodes end on a behaviour ("screenshot, block, tell one adult"). Wave 2, after a reviewer signs off the scripts and the app's crisis paths: "try Ward" and Give Ward to a friend.

options.label: Install CTA from the start
options.description: Every episode points to Ward straight away. Faster reach, but sends kids to crisis paths nobody has reviewed yet.

input.recap: The audit is saved outside the repo, and the lone-danger fix and the Discord no-nudge fix are on main (66580a5). Seven fixers are now running in their own worktrees, and the four pilot scripts are being written in Roman Urdu. Nothing from either workflow is merged yet.

content.text:
The audit is done and your four answers are in. Both work streams are running again after the earlier stop; nothing from them is merged yet.

**The audit:** the full report is [ward-audit-2026-10-31.md](../ward-audit-2026-10-31.md), next to your other posts and outside the public repo because it details security gaps that aren't fixed yet.
- **Strengths:** the safety rules are enforced in code and tests, privacy engineering is careful, failures are published honestly, and the evaluation hygiene is good.
- **The five biggest problems:**
  - **Gaps in the safety net:** a threat only Ward Lite catches could lose the strong help. A missed message has no path to help. Ward never notices the child's own distress, and reads a child quoting abuse as the bully.
  - **Shipped builds don't match what was tested:** CI-built APKs and installers ship without the files Ward Lite needs to run, so it silently doesn't. The APK won't install on 32-bit budget phones, every download link is a 404, and saving a chat longer than about 200 messages fails silently.
  - **Some public claims overstate the code,** including the report's "unchanged" check, which anyone could fake.
  - **The video campaign would run ahead of the app's own safeguarding review.**
  - **Discord server mode alerts adults,** against the written policy.

**Already fixed and pushed (`66580a5`):**
- A lone dangerous message in a one-to-one chat is now always urgent. Ward's second look can no longer clear a dangerous flag.
- Discord never nudges the sender of a dangerous message, so it can't tip off whoever is making threats or tell a child who's disclosing harm to delete it.

**Seven fixers now running,** each in its own worktree, each followed by a reviewer that tries to break the change and a follow-up pass on what it finds:
1. **Paths to help:** "It still feels wrong", a help door for every age, and full help for unconfirmed dangers (your answer). The correction-sharing copy stops pointing children to public GitHub.
2. **Helplines:** an unknown time zone no longer shows Pakistan's emergency number, and the child's region choice is saved.
3. **Builds and CI:** every build includes what Ward Lite needs to run, and CI checks it. CI runs the full test suite.
4. **Vault:** long chats save, and existing vaults keep opening.
5. **Docs:** honest wording on the report check, scorecard notes, install steps, and "build from source" until a release exists.
6. **Report:** an "unconfirmed" section (your answer), shown in the case viewer and counsellor mode. Existing reports still check.
7. **Discord:** server mode becomes a moderator tool, off by default (your answer), with its own policy section. It never shows the text of a self-harm alert, and it recognises children asking for help so it doesn't nudge them.

**The series:** the four pilot episodes (E1 the ghost on your side, E4 shut it down, E6 say it, E8 back them up) are being written in Roman Urdu, each with a kids' class cut and a teen social cut. Each script passes a safeguarding reviewer and a Roman Urdu reviewer, then a revision. They'll be in `ward-series/`, next to your other posts.

You chose to point to Ward from the start, so each episode ends on the behaviour first, then a short, honest line about Ward. In the kids' cuts that line speaks to the grown-ups watching.

One risk to know about: the app's crisis paths still haven't been reviewed by a safeguarding professional, and these videos will send children to them.

**Still yours to do:**
- **For the release (your choice: a preview after a real-phone test):** create the signing keystore with two offline backups, add the four GitHub secrets, and test on a real phone once the build fix lands.
- **Turn on private vulnerability reporting** on GitHub, and create safeguarding, security and conduct email addresses for the policy docs.
- **When you have time:** a contact at DRF or Madadgaar, how much time you can give Ward after the hackathon, and a content licence. The audit's question list has a recommended answer for each.

I'll merge, test and push each fix as it lands, then show you the scripts.

# E1 · The ghost on your side

Roman Urdu draft, for the owner's review. There are two cuts: a kids' cut and a teen cut. E1 has no single source story because it introduces who Ward is. Each cut is put together from existing stories, and every chat line comes from one of them (or replaces one with something milder), toned down to the mildest version. The story ids are listed so the script reviewer can check them against `stories.ts` and `stories.ur.ts`.

**Publishing gate (both cuts).** Do not post either cut until all of these are true:

- v0.1.0 is released with its published fingerprint, and the README badges and the Give QR resolve (no 404s).
- The landing page exists (Launch ring 1), so a parent or teen who looks Ward up finds a real page.
- The vault save fix has shipped, so saving a long class-group chat works and doesn't fail silently. Both cuts show saving to the vault as the core move.
- The reviewer sign-off (rule 10) is recorded, with the reviewer's name and date, for each cut separately.
- Teen cut only: the disclosure plan is ready (see the teen cut's Platform row).

**Ward on screen (new cast kind for the reel factory).** Ward is a small, soft, white ghost with a rounded top and a wavy hem. Its face is just two dot eyes and a small mouth. A warm amber glow (around `#ffb547`) surrounds it. It floats and never walks. It uses the app's own `Ghost.tsx` moods: `worried`, `calm`, `cheer`, `happy` and `think`. A proposed cast entry: `"ward": {"kind": "ghost", "color": "#ffffff", "glow": "#ffb547", "name": "Ward"}`. Ward never looks scary. In the kids' cut it fades in calm, beside the phone, as the room gets warmer.

**Grammar rule used throughout.** Ward (the ghost) takes masculine agreement in both cuts ("Ward dikhata hai", "Ward kisi ko kuch nahi batata"), so that it matches the end card. The viewer is never gendered. Every line addressed to "tum" uses imperatives ("karo", "lo", "chuno"), possessives that agree with the noun ("tumhari drawing", "tumhari side"), subject-free perfectives that agree with the object ("chat Ward ko dikhayi"), or the subject-free "hota hai" form.

**Spelling.** One Pakistani texting style throughout: bhari, jata, acha, choti, baray, walidain, bohat. Long vowels are doubled only where a word would otherwise be misread (aata, baat, baari, saaf).

---

## Cut 1: Kids

| | |
|---|---|
| **Title** | Ward: tumhari taraf wala bhoot (*Ward: the ghost on your side*) |
| **Cut** | Kids (8 to 12) |
| **Platform** | Made-for-kids YouTube (no comments, no end screens), plus the offline MP4 for the school kit / Class mode |
| **Length** | About 51 s in all: about 38 s of slow voice for the story (94 words at around 2.5 words per second), a silent 4 s freeze on the question, and a 10 s end card whose line is spoken. In class, the teacher can pause the freeze for as long as the vote takes. |
| **Source** | `now-you-see-it` (unit **save**, lesson `save-1` "Proof that sticks") supplies the two mean lines, the screenshot with name and time, Ammi, Ward's vault and Ms Farah. The sender is a made-up handle, **toofani_09**, instead of the story's Usman (see the safeguarding notes). The class-group setting ("Class 4 fun 🎉") comes from `mias-drawing` (unit **upstand**). The "tell a grown-up" beat comes from lesson `say-1` "Who's in your corner?" (unit **say**). |

### The hook (first thing on screen)

A phone lights up in a room lit by an evening lamp. The group name is **"Class 4 fun 🎉"** and a notification reads **"toofani_09: art mein tumhari drawing…"**

### Narration (Roman Urdu)

> Class group mein ek message aata hai. Phir ek aur.
> *A message arrives in the class group. Then another.*
>
> Dil bhari ho jata hai.
> *Your heart feels heavy.*
>
> Ab kya karna chahiye? A: jawab mein bura likho. B: chat delete karo. C: screenshot lo, kisi baray ko dikhao.
> *So what should you do now? A: write something mean in reply. B: delete the chat. C: take a screenshot and show a grown-up.*
>
> *(4 seconds of silence while the question stays on screen)*
>
> C. Screenshot lo, kisi baray ko dikhao.
> *C. Take a screenshot and show a grown-up.*
>
> Ammi ke saath, chat Ward ko dikhayi. Yeh Ward hai, tumhari taraf wala bhoot.
> *Together with Ammi, the chat is shown to Ward. This is Ward, the ghost on your side.*
>
> Do message, ek hi naam. Saboot lock ho jata hai.
> *Two messages, the same name. The proof gets locked away.*
>
> Is baar, agle din messages ruk gaye.
> *This time, the messages stopped the next day.*
>
> Reply mat karo. Screenshot lo. Kisi baray ko batao.
> *Don't reply. Take a screenshot. Tell a grown-up.*
>
> Walidain aur teachers: Ward free, open source hai, phone par chalta hai.
> *Parents and teachers: Ward is free and open source, and it runs on the phone.*
>
> *(over the end card, back in the child-facing voice)*
> Ward kisi ko kuch nahi batata. Isliye tum khud chuno, jis baray par bharosa ho, usko batao. Madad ke liye: 1098.
> *Ward never tells anyone. So you choose: tell a grown-up you trust. For help: 1098.*

Word count: 94 spoken words for the story, plus 21 over the end card.

### Scene by scene

Cast: `kid` is a bean person in a plain `hoodie`, colour `sage`, with no hair, bow, cap or other cues that read as a gender. The kid stands in for the viewer, so the narration never needs a pronoun. `ward` is the ghost. `ammi` is a person, colour `plum`. `farah` is a person, colour `slate`, with `glasses`. The sender, toofani_09, is a handle in the chat only and never appears as a character.

The four pilot scripts are written, each reviewed for safeguarding and for Roman Urdu, then revised. They're ready for you to read, and the code fixes are still running.

| Episode | Kids' cut (class / made-for-kids YouTube) | Teen cut (TikTok / Reels / Shorts) |
|---|---|---|
| [E1 · The ghost on your side](../ward-series/E1-ward-on-your-side.md) | A class group message, a vote ("A, B ya C?"), then Ammi and Ward keep the proof | "Bullying = chat ka bhoot": a pile-on, keep proof, choose one person to tell |
| [E4 · Shut it down](../ward-series/E4-shut-it-down.md) | *The treehouse*: someone wrecks your build in a game, so don't reply, save it, block | Replying feeds it: keep proof, block, report. Says "already replied? that's OK" |
| [E6 · Say it](../ward-series/E6-say-it.md) | *The tablet worry*: the fear that telling means losing the tablet; also tells parents "say thank you, don't take the tablet away" | If one adult doesn't help, tell another |
| [E8 · Back them up](../ward-series/E8-back-them-up.md) | *Mia's drawing*: one kind message, sent privately | *The poll*: don't vote, don't share, message the person privately, report it |

**What each file contains, per cut:**
- the hook
- the Roman Urdu narration, with an English line under each line
- a scene-by-scene table in your reel factory's format: set, cast, mood, pose, speech bubbles of six words or fewer, props, cue phrases
- the call to action and end card
- safeguarding notes, and notes for recording the voice
- a "Review notes" section listing what the reviewers changed

**Things to decide as you read:**
- **Length:** the kids' cuts run 51 to 60 seconds, over the 45-second target. The time goes on the four-second vote freeze and a spoken helpline, and the writers kept those on purpose. You may prefer shorter.
- **Spelling:** the episodes don't agree. Some use "bade", some "baray". Pick one and I'll make them all match.
- **Ward is "he" in Urdu** ("Ward dikhata hai"), matching the app's voice. The child watching is never given a gender: every line to them uses forms like "karo" and "lo".
- **Ward as a character:** each file describes Ward as a new reel factory character, a small white ghost with an amber glow that floats and uses the app's ghost moods. Your pipeline needs that character added before rendering.
- **Ward pointer:** you chose to point to Ward from the start. Each cut ends on the behaviour first, then one honest line about Ward, and in the kids' cuts that line speaks to parents and teachers.
- **When to post:** each file lists conditions to meet before posting:
  - a real release, so links aren't dead ends
  - the long-chat save fix shipped, since the videos show saving to the vault
  - a reviewer's sign-off on each cut
  - for teen cuts, a plan for replying to comments where a child discloses harm

  E8 also asks for the Discord and pairing fixes first. You can relax any of these, but they reflect what the videos promise.

When you've read them, tell me what to change in the voice, the slang or the scenes. Then I'll turn E1 into a reel factory storyboard and add the ghost character to your pipeline, so you can render a first preview without spending voice credits.

The seven code fixers are still working in their worktrees. I'll merge, test and push each one as it finishes.

input.recap: All seven audit fixes are merged and pushed (5da5f77), and every test passes locally. The Roman Urdu pilot scripts are ready to review in ward-series/. The CI, Android and desktop builds are still running.

content.text:
All seven audit fixes are merged and pushed (`5da5f77`). Each was reviewed by an agent trying to break it, then followed up. All tests pass locally (42 root tests plus 48 package tests), the type checks pass, and the web build now includes Ward Lite's runtime. CI, Android and desktop builds are running on GitHub to confirm.

**What's now on main:**
- **Paths to help:**
  - A "Need someone to talk to?" door on Home for every age (I checked it in the app).
  - "It still feels wrong" on calm results.
  - Full help for messages Ward isn't sure about, as you chose: helplines, Take It Down, the Coach and the safety plan, under the "not sure" heading.
  - Correcting a message to something worse brings help up.
  - "This looks okay" no longer shows while Ward is still reading.
  - Corrections stay on the phone, and nothing points children to GitHub any more.
- **Helplines:** an unknown time zone no longer shows Pakistan's emergency number. The child's region choice is saved, and the school kit lets the teacher pick.
- **Builds:** every build now includes what Ward Lite needs to run. The Android and desktop builds check for it, the desktop smoke test checks Ward Lite actually opens, and CI runs the full test suite.
- **Vault:** chats of any length save, old vaults still open, a failed save says so calmly, and the PIN pad can't freeze.
- **Report:** messages Ward isn't sure about go in their own "Not confirmed by Ward" section in the report, the case viewer and counsellor mode, as you chose. Existing reports still check.
- **Discord:** server mode is a moderator tool, off by default, with its own section in the safeguarding policy. Self-harm alerts never show the message text. A child reporting abuse ("someone told me…") is never nudged or named as the sender.
- **Honest docs:** the report check now says it catches accidental damage and casual edits, not a determined forger. The README says "build from source" until a release exists, the scorecard notes are fixed, and the macOS 15 and Windows install steps are current.

Your bot is running on the new code. I switched server mode on for your testing, since it's off by default now.

**Decisions the fixers raised:**
1. **Gemma downgrading a dangerous phrase.** When Gemma reads a phrase like "kys" as a joke, the engine lowers it from dangerous to hurtful, and the helplines block disappears. That goes against the "safety only goes up" rule. My recommendation: keep it dangerous, but label it "may be a joke". It's documented in SAFEGUARDING.md for the safeguarding review.
2. **Discord trade-off.** To make sure sextortion threats always alert, a message containing "you", "tu", "or else" or "warna" counts as aimed at someone. So a child quoting abuse ("usne mujhe kaha tu mar ja") could be named in a full mod alert. Self-harm alerts never name anyone, and server mode is off by default.
3. **Wording to sign off:** the new "Not confirmed by Ward" explanation, and the app's "nothing around it looks unkind" line. History records an unconfirmed danger as "Keep an eye" rather than adding a new level.
4. **Failed vault save:** should the child be able to make a report straight from the result when saving to the vault fails?
5. **The privacy line.** "A child's messages never leave the device" is false when a phone is paired with a family computer. The docs fixer applied a more accurate line in the README, and some in-app strings still use the old one. It's your sentence to choose, and it's also the line the reels will use.

**Scripts:** the four pilot episodes are in Roman Urdu in [ward-series/](../ward-series/E1-ward-on-your-side.md), waiting for your read.

**Still yours to do:**
- **Release:** create the signing keystore with two offline backups and add the four GitHub secrets. Then test on a real phone and I'll tag the v0.1.0 preview.
- **Security reporting:** turn on GitHub's private vulnerability reporting, and create the safeguarding, security and conduct email addresses.

I'll report the CI, Android and desktop results when they finish.

# AI Reel Factory (@hussainreflections)

A local-first tool that turns an AI/tech idea into a finished 1080×1920 Instagram Reel: animated character
story scenes, the owner's ElevenLabs voice clone, kinetic captions, music, a CTA end card and a cover.
The README has the full guide; `docs/story-scenes.md` is the storyboard reference.

## Making a reel

Use the `/reel` skill (`.claude/skills/reel/SKILL.md`). In short:
`new-idea` → write `data/scripts/<ID>.json` with `"draft": true` → `check` → `preview --dry` → user OK →
`ready` → the watcher (or `voice` + `render`) → Telegram review → user approves and posts by hand.

`RF` = `.venv/bin/python -m reelfactory`. Useful commands: `ideas`, `new-idea`, `check`, `preview --dry`, `ready`,
`voice`, `render`, `status`, `inbox`, `approve`, `published`, `doctor`. Tests: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q`.

## Rules set by the owner

- **Paid services:** ElevenLabs Starter is the only one (TTS with their clone, plus a one-off Eleven Music library). Add nothing else that costs money.
- **Claude:** no Claude API calls from scripts. Claude is used interactively only, on the owner's Max plan.
- **Publishing:** never post to Instagram automatically.
- **Voice:** real reels use only the owner's voice clone or their own recording.
- **Credits:** each voiceover costs about 450 characters. Never re-voice (`--force`) without asking.
- **Visual style:** character-driven story scenes, not text cards. Keep on-screen text short and keep "follow me" out of the script.
- **Stack:** the API and n8n run as a LaunchAgent (`scripts/install-launchd.sh`). Restart it after code changes with `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.reelfactory.stack`.
- **Network:** everything stays on 127.0.0.1. Secrets stay in the git-ignored `.env`.
- **Volume:** 3 reels a day. The owner also sends their own ideas as `.md` files (drop them in `inbox/ideas/`).

---
name: reel
description: Make one Instagram Reel for your account (handle and niche in config/style.json) end to end, from a shortlist number, an idea .md file, an existing AI-… ID or a pasted idea. It fact-checks the source, writes the script and the animated story storyboard, runs the pre-flight check, previews stills without spending credits, then hands off to voice + render once the user approves. Use for "/reel", "make a reel about…", "next reel", "today's reels".
---

# /reel: one Reel, from idea to rendered draft

Work in `~/Projects/reel-factory` (`~/Desktop/frf` is a shortcut to it). `RF` below means `.venv/bin/python -m reelfactory`, run from that folder.

## 1. Find the idea

| The user gave | Do |
|---|---|
| nothing | Show `RF ideas` plus the top 5 of the newest `data/scripts/shortlist-*.md`, and ask which one |
| a number `N` | `RF new-idea N` (rank in the latest shortlist) |
| a `.md` path, or a file name in `inbox/ideas/` | `RF new-idea <file>` (the note is filed under `inbox/ideas/used/`) |
| pasted text / a topic | Write it to `inbox/ideas/<short-slug>.md` (first line `# <title>`, keep their words and links), then `RF new-idea <slug>.md` |
| an ID like `AI-20261020-004` | Carry on with that storyboard |

`new-idea` prints the new ID, the storyboard path `data/scripts/<ID>.json` and the brief `data/scripts/<ID>.brief.md`.

## 2. Read before writing

- The brief `data/scripts/<ID>.brief.md` is the spec: word count, scene rules, vocabulary, layout limits.
- `docs/story-scenes.md` is the full element reference.
- Use one recently rendered storyboard as a pattern (`RF status`, pick the newest `rendered` AI-… ID, then read its JSON).
- The ig-* skills in `~/.claude/skills` (`IG` below) do the Instagram craft. Read `~/.claude/instagram/voice.md` (the owner's voice), `IG/ig-reel/hooks.json` (26 hook formulas) and, if it exists, `~/.claude/instagram/swipe.md` (what `/ig-viral` found working in the niche; it beats the defaults).

## 3. Research

- Fetch every source URL. Write down 3–5 facts, each with the exact supporting quote.
- If the note has no source, search for a reliable one. If you can't find one, tell the user and stop.
- Anything you can't tie to a quote is `uncertain`. Don't hype, and use only verified facts in the script.

## 4. Write the storyboard

- Write 3 hook options (under 10 words each) off three different formulas in `hooks.json`, one per line in a scratch file, and rank them with `python3 IG/ig-reel/hookscore.py <file>`. The script's first sentence is the hook. Under 50 means there is no hook yet: rewrite, don't polish. Pick the top one and say why in one line.

- Show the idea instead of printing it: characters act each beat, props appear when they're mentioned, and the camera pushes in on the key moment. Keep on-screen text to short labels, counters, stamps or one title. Visuals must not imply numbers the source doesn't give.
- Save the storyboard with the Write tool to `data/scripts/<ID>.json`.

## 5. Check, then look

1. `RF check <ID>`: fix every FAIL. Fix WARNs too when it's cheap to do so (layout, cue timing, thumbnail). Repeat until it prints `READY TO VOICE`. The last three lines are the ig-* scores (`hook score`, `human score`, `caption lint`); a WEAK hook is worth fixing before any credits are spent.
2. `RF preview <ID> --dry`: open `output/drafts/<ID>.preview.jpg` and `output/.work/<ID>/preview/cover.jpg` with Read, and review them critically:
   - Does every beat show something happening?
   - Is there any empty or crowded scene, or overlapping actors and props?
   - Is anything sitting under the caption band at the top?
   - Is the text readable, and the cover readable at grid size?
   Fix the storyboard, re-check and re-preview. Stop after about 3 rounds.

## 6. Show the user and wait

Send the preview sheet with SendUserFile. Then give, briefly:
- the chosen hook (and the other two), each with its formula and hook score

### Call to action and end card

**Behaviour (spoken, and the title of scene 8):** "Reply mat karo. Screenshot lo. Kisi baray ko batao." (*Don't reply. Take a screenshot. Tell a grown-up.*)

**Pointer (spoken to the adults only):** "Walidain aur teachers: Ward free, open source hai, phone par chalta hai." The story has just shown what Ward does (it notices the pattern, keeps the proof and leaves the telling to the child), so the pointer doesn't repeat it.

**End card (spoken over a hold of at least 10 s, so it works with no end screens and for children who can't read it in time):**

> **Ward kisi ko kuch nahi batata. Isliye tum khud chuno, jis baray par bharosa ho, usko batao.**
> *Ward never tells anyone, so you choose: tell a grown-up you trust.*
>
> **Pakistan:** Madadgaar **1098**
> **Pakistan:** DRF Cyber Harassment Helpline **0800-39393** (Peer se Jumma, subah 9 se shaam 5)
> **India:** **1098** · **Bangladesh:** **1098**
> **Kahin aur:** findahelpline.com

Spoken: the bold line, then "Madad ke liye: 1098."

### Safeguarding notes

- **No install pitch to children.** The child is never told to use Ward. Sign C and the spoken answer are word for word the same ("Screenshot lo, kisi baray ko dikhao"), so the right answer is the grown-up, not the app. Ward comes in only after the child has gone to Ammi, and it is opened together with her ("Ammi ke saath, chat Ward ko dikhayi"). The only Ward pointer is spoken to "walidain aur teachers". There is no "download", no link, no QR code and no store badge. The reel factory's Follow end card must be switched off for this cut (`"cta": false`).
- **The voice ends on the child.** The last spoken words are the end card's trusted-grown-up line and 1098, not the Ward pointer.
- **No real name for the sender.** The source story's sender is Usman, a very common name. If the MP4 plays in a real Class 4, a classmate with that name could be teased. The sender is a made-up handle (toofani_09), and the narration says "ek message" and "ek hi naam" instead of a name. School-kit teacher note: "The sender is a made-up handle. Please don't let the class guess who it 'is'."
- **Mildest lines only.** I used the drawing line and the egg line from `now-you-see-it`. I left out "nobody wants to sit next to you tomorrow", which is an exclusion line that hurts more than the others. The mean lines appear only on the phone and are never spoken, so the voice doesn't give them any extra weight.
- **No vanishing-message trick.** The source story is built around deleted messages. That is a second idea, and it can confuse an 8-year-old in a short video. It belongs in E5.
- **No confrontation.** The "send it to them: I saw it" branch is left out. The proof goes to grown-ups, as the source's kind ending teaches.
- **The sender is not a monster.** It never appears as a character and gets no scary styling. The kids' cut deliberately avoids any "bully" or "ghost in the chat" line, because a classmate shouldn't be turned into a villain in front of a class.
- **Ward never looks scary.** The lights warm up rather than dip, and Ward fades in calm beside the phone instead of rising out of it.
- **No "protects" or "keeps safe".** Ward shows ("Do message, ek hi naam") and the proof is locked ("Saboot lock ho jata hai"). There is no shield prop, because a shield reads as protection. The lock stands for the vault's PIN and nothing more.
- **Ward doesn't appear by magic.** The chat is shown to Ward on purpose, because Ward only reads what the child chooses to share with it.
- **The vote is gender-neutral.** "Ab kya karna chahiye?" avoids "tum kya karte/karti".
- **No engagement pressure.** No "part 2" and no "subscribe". The YouTube made-for-kids settings mean there are no comments or end screens.
- **The ending is honest.** "Is baar, agle din messages ruk gaye" is in the past tense and tied to this story ("is baar"), so it isn't a promise that telling always works. E7 covers what to do when it doesn't stop.

### For the voice

- Speak like an older cousin sitting next to the child, not like a teacher at the front of the class. Keep it warm, slow and low.
- Pace: about 2.5 words per second. Leave a full beat after "Dil bhari ho jata hai."
- Read A, B and C evenly, without hinting at the right answer, and then actually stop. The 4 s of silence is part of the episode.
- Read the reveal "C. Screenshot lo, kisi baray ko dikhao" exactly as the sign says, so voters can match it.
- Lift your voice slightly on "Yeh Ward hai", like introducing a friend.
- Read the pointer, to parents and teachers, in a plain, adult voice. Change tone a little so children can hear that it isn't aimed at them. Then go back to the cousin voice for the end card line, and say "1098" slowly, digit by digit: "ek, sifar, nau, aath".
- Pronunciation: "Ward" rhymes with "lord", not "wad". Say "baray" as *ba-ṛay*, with the retroflex flap.
- **Recording tip:** record in a quiet room 10 to 15 cm from the mic. Then save the take as `inbox/voiceovers/<ID>.m4a`. The factory's whisper model is `ggml-base.en`, which is English-only, so word timing on Roman Urdu will probably fall back to silence detection. Either keep clear pauses between the lines above, or switch to the multilingual `ggml-base.bin` for these episodes. Every cue phrase in the table appears word for word in the narration.

content.text:
The first episode renders. I sent you the preview sheet and the end card: the E1 kids' cut, a dry run from your reel factory, so no voice credits were spent.

**The secrets.** You already made everything on 29 October; it's in `Hacktoberfest 26/ward-android-signing/`. From the `ward` folder, run these four commands. Each pipes the value straight into GitHub, so the password is never printed.

```bash
base64 -i "../ward-android-signing/ward-release.p12" | gh secret set ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64
```

```bash
tr -d '\n' < "../ward-android-signing/password.txt" | gh secret set ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD
```

```bash
printf REDACTED | gh secret set ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS
```

```bash
tr -d '\n' < "../ward-android-signing/password.txt" | gh secret set ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD
```

Then `gh secret list` should show all four. Back up that folder in two places, for example your password manager and a USB drive. Losing the key means Ward can never install as an update again.

**Your decision is in (`998c5d2`):** when Gemma reads dangerous words as a joke, the message stays dangerous and the help stays on screen, with the note "It may be a joke, but these words are serious." It's tested and pushed.

**The series has started.** In `~/Projects/reel-factory`:
- **Ward the ghost is a new character:** a small white floating ghost with a soft amber glow. It uses your existing moods and poses: "wave" and "cheer" bob, "panic" shivers.
- **A new `chat` prop:** a phone showing a group chat in a made-up messenger that doesn't look like any real app. Bubbles wrap and type in, and lines can light up amber when Ward points out the pattern.
- **Series settings per storyboard:** a storyboard can set its own word range, its own handle (E1 shows "Ward · free, open source" instead of @hussainreflections) and `"cta": false` to turn off the Follow card.
- **Tests:** all 200 of your reel factory's tests pass. I committed only those four source files locally and didn't push your repo.

The E1 kids' storyboard is `data/scripts/WARD-E1-KIDS.json`. It passes your pipeline's check except for the Instagram scoring warnings, which are tuned for English AI reels. The preview shows the whole story:
- the class group messages
- the A, B, C vote
- the child showing Ammi
- Ward fading in: "Main yahin hoon."
- the two messages lighting up, with "Tumhari ghalti nahi hai"
- Ms Farah at school
- the takeaway: "Reply mat karo. Screenshot lo. Kisi baray ko batao."
- the line for parents and teachers
- the helpline end card, with Madadgaar 1098 largest

**Before a full render, two things from your side:**
- **Your voice.** Record the narration from the E1 script and save it as `inbox/voiceovers/WARD-E1-KIDS.m4a`, following its voice notes: about 2.5 words a second, a real four-second pause after the vote, and 1098 read digit by digit.
- **Roman Urdu caption timing.** Your factory times captions with an English-only whisper model. I'd download the multilingual model (`ggml-base.bin`, about 148 MB) so the words line up with your Urdu speech.

"""Word timing: whisper.cpp word timestamps aligned to the script, with a
silence-detection fallback when whisper is unavailable."""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
from dataclasses import dataclass, asdict
from difflib import SequenceMatcher
from pathlib import Path

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)


@dataclass
class Word:
    text: str          # display text, punctuation kept
    start: float
    end: float

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        return asdict(self)


def normalize(word: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]", "", word.lower().replace("’", "'"))


def tokenize_script(script: str) -> list[str]:
    return [w for w in script.replace("“", '"').replace("”", '"').split() if normalize(w)]


def probe_duration(path: Path) -> float:
    out = subprocess.run(
        ["ffprobe", "-v", "error", "-show_entries", "format=duration", "-of", "json", str(path)],
        capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
    return float(json.loads(out)["format"]["duration"])


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- whisper


def whisper_available(model: Path) -> bool:
    return shutil.which("whisper-cli") is not None and model.exists()


def transcribe_whisper(audio: Path, model: Path, threads: int = 8) -> list[Word]:
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
        wav = Path(td) / "a16k.wav"
        subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-y", "-i", str(audio), "-ar", "16000", "-ac", "1", str(wav)],
                       check=True)
        out = Path(td) / "w"
        subprocess.run(["whisper-cli", "-m", str(model), "-f", str(wav), "-ml", "1", "-sow", "-oj",
                        "-of", str(out), "-np", "-t", str(threads), "-l", "en"],
                       check=True, capture_output=True)
        data = json.loads((out.with_suffix(".json")).read_text())
    words = []
    for seg in data.get("transcription", []):
        t = seg["text"].strip()
        if not normalize(t):
            continue
        words.append(Word(t, seg["offsets"]["from"] / 1000, seg["offsets"]["to"] / 1000))
    return words


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- fallback


def speech_segments(audio: Path, noise_db: float = -35, min_silence: float = 0.18) -> list[tuple[float, float]]:
    """Non-silent intervals via ffmpeg silencedetect."""
    dur = probe_duration(audio)
    res = subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-hide_banner", "-i", str(audio), "-af",
                          f"silencedetect=noise={noise_db}dB:d={min_silence}", "-f", "null", "-"],
                         capture_output=True, text=True)
    starts = [float(x) for x in re.findall(r"silence_start: ([\d.]+)", res.stderr)]
    ends = [float(x) for x in re.findall(r"silence_end: ([\d.]+)", res.stderr)]
    silences = list(zip(starts, ends + [dur] * (len(starts) - len(ends))))
    segs, cur = [], 0.0
    for s, e in silences:
        if s - cur > 0.05:
            segs.append((cur, s))
        cur = e
    if dur - cur > 0.05:
        segs.append((cur, dur))
    return segs or [(0.0, dur)]


def distribute(script_words: list[str], segments: list[tuple[float, float]]) -> list[Word]:
    """Spread words over speech segments weighted by character length."""
    weights = [len(normalize(w)) + 1.5 for w in script_words]
    total_w = sum(weights)
    total_t = sum(e - s for s, e in segments)
    words, acc = [], 0.0

    def to_time(pos: float) -> float:
        for s, e in segments:
            if pos <= e - s:
                return s + pos
            pos -= e - s
        return segments[-1][1]

    for w, wt in zip(script_words, weights):
        a = acc / total_w * total_t
        acc += wt
        b = acc / total_w * total_t
        words.append(Word(w, to_time(a), to_time(b - 1e-6)))
    return words


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- alignment


def align(script_words: list[str], heard: list[Word], duration: float) -> tuple[list[Word], float]:
    """Give each script word a time using matched transcript words; interpolate the rest.

    Returns (timed words, match ratio 0..1).
    """
    a = [normalize(w) for w in script_words]
    b = [normalize(w.text) for w in heard]
    sm = SequenceMatcher(a=a, b=b, autojunk=False)
    times: list[tuple[float, float] | None] = [None] * len(a)
    matched = 0
    for blk in sm.get_matching_blocks():
        for k in range(blk.size):
            hw = heard[blk.b + k]
            times[blk.a + k] = (hw.start, hw.end)
            matched += 1

"""Voice a Ward episode with Meta's open MMS Urdu TTS, line by line, and write word timing for the
Roman Urdu captions. Usage: python voice_mms.py <lines.json> <out.wav>
lines.json: [{"roman": "...", "urdu": "...", "pause": seconds_after}, ...]"""
import json
import re
import sys

import numpy as np
import scipy.io.wavfile as wavfile
import torch
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, VitsModel

lines = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
out_wav = sys.argv[2]
torch.manual_seed(7)
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("facebook/mms-tts-urd-script_arabic")
model = VitsModel.from_pretrained("facebook/mms-tts-urd-script_arabic")
model.speaking_rate = 0.92  # a little slower, for children
sr = model.config.sampling_rate


def norm(w):
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]", "", w.lower().replace("’", "'"))


audio, words, t = [np.zeros(int(0.35 * sr), dtype=np.float32)], [], 0.35
for ln in lines:
    with torch.no_grad():
        wav = model(**tok(ln["urdu"], return_tensors="pt")).waveform[0].numpy()
    # trim the model's own leading/trailing near-silence so the timing is tight
    idx = np.where(np.abs(wav) > 0.02)[0]
    if len(idx):
        wav = wav[max(0, idx[0] - int(0.03 * sr)): idx[-1] + int(0.05 * sr)]
    dur = len(wav) / sr
    toks = [w for w in ln["roman"].split() if norm(w)]
    weights = [len(norm(w)) + 1.5 for w in toks]
    acc, total = 0.0, sum(weights)
    for w, wt in zip(toks, weights):
        a = t + acc / total * dur
        acc += wt
        words.append({"text": w, "start": round(a, 3), "end": round(t + acc / total * dur, 3)})
    audio += [wav, np.zeros(int(ln["pause"] * sr), dtype=np.float32)]
    t += dur + ln["pause"]
    print(f"{dur:5.2f}s  {ln['roman']}")

pcm = np.concatenate(audio)
pcm = pcm / max(1e-6, np.abs(pcm).max()) * 0.9
wavfile.write(out_wav, sr, (pcm * 32767).astype(np.int16))
json.dump(words, open(out_wav.rsplit(".", 1)[0] + ".words.json", "w"), ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)
print(f"total {t:.2f}s, {len(words)} words")

def frame_svg(t: float, tl: Timeline, style: dict, show_captions: bool = True) -> str:
    W, H = style["width"], style["height"]
    T = style.get("transition_seconds", 0.28)
    i = tl.scene_at(t)
    cur = tl.scenes[i]
    layers = [sc.background(t, style)]

    def draw(idx: int) -> str:
        s = tl.scenes[idx]
        return sc.SCENES[s.type](t - s.start, s.dur, s.params, style)

    in_tr = i > 0 and t < cur.start + T
    if in_tr:
        e = (t - cur.start) / T
        layers += transition(cur.params.get("transition") or ("zoom" if cur.type == "story" else "fade"),
                             e, draw(i - 1), draw(i), W, H)
    else:
        layers.append(draw(i))
    if hasattr(sc, "chrome"):
        layers.append(sc.chrome(style))
    kinetic = style["captions"].get("mode") == "kinetic"
    if show_captions and not _title_on(cur, t - cur.start) and not (kinetic and cur.type == "endcard"):
        layers.append(cap.render(t, tl.chunks, style))
    return svg.document(W, H, sc.defs(style), "".join(layers))


def _title_on(scene, lt: float) -> bool:
    """Story scenes hide the captions while their big title is on screen."""
    if scene.type != "story":
        return False
    from . import story
def render_frames(tl: Timeline, style: dict, paths: Paths, frame_dir: Path, workers: int | None = None) -> int:
    if frame_dir.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(frame_dir)
    frame_dir.mkdir(parents=True)
    n_frames = int(round(tl.duration * style["fps"]))
    workers = workers or int(os.environ.get("REELFACTORY_WORKERS", os.cpu_count() or 4))
    t0 = time.time()
    with Pool(workers, initializer=_init, initargs=(tl, style, rsvg_env(paths), frame_dir, paths.fonts)) as pool:
        for k, _ in enumerate(pool.imap_unordered(_render_one, range(n_frames), chunksize=4), 1):
            if k % 150 == 0 or k == n_frames:
                log.info("frames %d/%d (%.1fs)", k, n_frames, time.time() - t0)
    return n_frames


def encode(frame_dir: Path, audio_wav: Path, out_mp4: Path, fps: int, duration: float) -> Path:
    out_mp4.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    tmp = out_mp4.with_suffix(".partial.mp4")
    cmd = ["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-y", "-framerate", str(fps), "-i", str(frame_dir / "%05d.png"),
           "-i", str(audio_wav), "-map", "0:v", "-map", "1:a",
           "-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "medium", "-crf", "18", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p",
           "-profile:v", "high", "-r", str(fps), "-g", str(fps * 2),
           "-c:a", "aac", "-b:a", "192k", "-ar", "48000",
           "-t", f"{duration:.3f}", "-movflags", "+faststart", str(tmp)]
    subprocess.run(cmd, check=True, capture_output=True, text=True)
    tmp.replace(out_mp4)
    return out_mp4


def _save_jpg(svg_text: str, paths: Paths, out_jpg: Path) -> Path:

    Image.open(png).convert("RGB").save(out_jpg, quality=92)
    png.unlink()
    return out_jpg

- is voiced in Urdu with Meta's open model, with Roman Urdu captions timed to the voice

| Discord bot | Your Mac | Running locally. `render.yaml` exists but isn't deployed |

**Partner technology: planned vs actual**

| Partner | Plan | Status | What's left to implement |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Gemma** | Everything that reads | ✅ Done | Gemma 4 E4B via Ollama and built into desktop (llama.cpp), E2B on phones, Gemma as Ward Lite's teacher, the second-look reader. Only the scorecard's Gemma rows need re-running |
| **ElevenLabs** | Read-aloud narration | ⚠️ Half | 107 English clips shipped. Urdu clips not made, and the account is at 0 credits. Blocked until credits return |
| **Entire** | Session checkpoints | ✅ Enabled | Imported once earlier. Re-import this session's later work before submitting |
| **Render** | Host the demo, case viewer, docs and Discord bot | ❌ Not deployed | 1. A static site for the web app as a try-it demo, with a strict CSP. 2. The case viewer as a static page. 3. The Discord bot as a worker, already described in `render.yaml` (about $7/month, personal mode only, per your decision). Needs you to connect Render (`/mcp` in a terminal) or click New → Blueprint |
| **DigitalOcean** | A GPU droplet for synthetic data, a bigger teacher model, scorecard runs | ❌ Not started | Not really needed now: training ran fine on your Mac. Only worth it for Ward Lite v2 with context |
| **Browserbase + SerpApi** | A weekly job checking that each app's report and block help pages still match the Coach's steps | ❌ Not started | A scheduled GitHub Action: SerpApi finds the official help pages, Browserbase loads them, and differences open an issue. Needs API keys from both, which you'd add as secrets |
| **Auth0** | Logins for Ward Annotate volunteers | ⏸ Later | Depends on building Annotate, which needs a safeguarding lead first |
| **Tiger Data** | Scorecard and red-team history across releases | ⏸ Later | Small: push each eval run's results into a Timescale table and chart regressions |

content.text:
The real Gemma demo is live and working.

**What's deployed:**
- **Website** (https://ward-w8cd.onrender.com): when a visitor's check finishes, a "Try the close read with Gemma" card appears, in English and Urdu, with a "Read it with Gemma (demo)" button. It says plainly that this sends the chat to Ward's demo server and to use the example chat. Real installs of Ward never show it.
- **Relay** on the bot service (`ward-discord.onrender.com/gemma`): it calls Gemma on Google AI Studio with your key, which stays server-side. It picked **Gemma 4 31B**.
  - **Other websites refused:** a request from any other site gets a 403, which I checked.
  - **Rate-limited:** small requests only, 40 per visitor every 10 minutes.
  - **Nothing kept:** no text is logged and nothing is stored.
  - **Two fixes:** it now sends back only Gemma's answer, not its thinking, and retries once when Google returns a server error.

**End-to-end test:** I ran Ward's own engine against the live relay, using the same reader and the same requests the website sends. Gemma read the whole example chat with context:
- **Verdict:** "urgent", the correct reading for this chat.
- **Notes in plain words,** for example "Calls Ayesha a buffalo to mock their weight" and "Suggests removing Ayesha from the group."
- **Zara, who stood up for Ayesha, wasn't flagged.**

**Not tested:** the button itself in a browser. The browser pane here blocks requests to the relay's second address, so I tested the same code path from Node instead. Clicking it in your own browser will confirm it.

**Speed:** that read took about **2 minutes** for 16 messages. The 31B model is large and thinks before answering, and the page shows progress while it works. Your key also has a second Gemma model, likely a faster one. Switching is one Render setting (`GEMMA_MODEL`), and I'd check it reads the example chat just as well before swapping.
Yes, make it faster
To switch, I need the second model's exact name. The relay only logged the one it picked, so I'm making it log both names (no key or text involved):
